title: Performance to Assurance: One‑Pager for Core Positioning
purpose: Concise internal brief to align messaging that moves conversations from raw model capability to predictable, production-grade inference assurance for engineering buyers.
mission_statement: Make high-performance LLM inference reliably predictable and economically accessible so engineering teams can ship features with confidence, not guesswork.
thesis: Competitive advantage shifts from model ownership to serving guarantees. Teams care less about marginal model accuracy and more about consistent latency, predictable cost, and resilient behavior under real traffic. Redwood converts model potential into repeatable product outcomes through an inference-first platform.
why_redwood: Redwood unifies a GPU-optimized serving runtime, intelligent routing, and operational tooling so teams get consistent latency and unit economics across hosted, reserved, and private deployments. We don’t just expose models — we manage the operational complexity that makes LLM features reliable in production.
prop_bullets: Predictable latency SLOs with multi-tier fallback policies (region/model/capacity).
Cost controls: batching, prefix caching, and quantization recommendations tied to real workload profiles.
One API, three deployment modes: Hosted for speed, Dedicated for capacity predictability, Private for compliance and isolation.
Observability that maps quality regressions to prompt sets, model versions, and rollout events (traceable, actionable alerts).
Runtime-level performance tuning (kernel selection + memory management) that reduces per-token cost without manual optimization work.
competitive_differentiation: Vs general cloud AI endpoints: We provide end-to-end inference economics (latency + per-token cost) and built-in fallbacks — not just a VM with a model.
Vs LLM API-only vendors: Our emphasis is on predictable service primitives (SLOs, rollouts, cost levers) that match product team needs rather than raw convenience calls.

Vs inference self-hosted vendors: We combine a battle-tested runtime with hosted ops and private deployment options — customers can start simple and graduate to isolated deployments without rewriting integrations.
proof_points: Customer X reduced median tail latency 3x by switching to Redwood routing + KV prefix caching in production.
Beta test: average per-token cost reduction of 28% after applying our Optimize recommendations on a high-concurrency chat workload.
Dedicated customers report predictable throughput during seasonal spikes because of reserved pool autoscaling policies and burst lanes.
sales_talking_points: Engineering buyers: 'We’ll sign up if your SLOs map to our SLA and we can avoid surprise spend.' — Lead with telemetry, rollout controls, and transparent unit economics.
Platform teams: 'We need a repeatable runtime others on the org can adopt.' — Emphasize unified APIs across modes and migration story from hosted to private.
Security/compliance: 'Can we run in our VPC/on-prem and keep auditability?' — Highlight private deployment controls, KMS integrations, and audit logs.
objections_and_rebuttals: Objection: 'We can tune open-source models ourselves.' — Rebuttal: Tuning is ongoing; Redwood operationalizes tuning into stable SLOs and provides continuous workload-aware kernel/quantization suggestions backed by telemetry.

Objection: 'Vendor lock-in concerns.' — Rebuttal: API compatibility across hosted/dedicated/private and model-variant fallbacks reduce migration cost; we surface configuration and manifests so teams own the rollout artifacts.
Objection: 'Price looks higher than raw infra.' — Rebuttal: Show variance-adjusted unit economics and the hidden ops/engineering cost of maintaining equivalent latency/reliability in-house.
next_steps: Finalize one-pager language for customer-facing handoff (deadline 2025-02-10).
